caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 159 of 2005
lawyer:
B. Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners. 
Respondent(s) ------ Not represented.
parties:
The Deputy Commissioner, Comilla and others ------ Petitioners.
VS
Md. Asimuddin and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment: 3. The respondent No.1 filed the above suit for declaration that the notice dated 12.5.99 issued by the Chairman, Borura Pourashava, Comilla directing him to take away his tinshed house from the suit land is illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon him stating, inter alia, that the suit land measuring 6 decimals along with other lands were recorded in the name of Raja Krishna Das Laha and on promulgation of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the suit land along with other lands were recorded in Khas Khatian No.1; thereafter he and some other persons who were in possession of those land applied for settlement of said lands in their favour and the then Sub-Divisional Officer, Comilla, on 25.9.74, gave settlement of the suit land measuring 6 decimals to him through a registered lease deed dated 30.11.74 vide Settlement Case No. 20 of 1972-73 and others who were also in possession of land like the plaintiff also got settlements of the remaining lands; then Khatian No. 558 was prepared in the name of the plaintiff and he had been praying rents to government; thereafter on 21.7.76 the then Sub-Divisional Officer (South), Comilla cancelled the settlement vide Settlement Review Case No.1 of 1976-77 whereupon he filed Misc. Appeal No. 7 of 1976-77) to A.D.C.(Revenue), Comilla which was rejected; then he filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Borura for declaration of title and further relief that the above order of cancellation dated 21.7.76 is illegal, ineffective and not binding upon him and the said suit being dismissed on 28.5.91 he filed Title Appeal No. 175 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge, Comilla and the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Comilla, after hearing, by judgment and decree dated 23.3.1997 allowed the appeal and thereby the above order dated 21.7.76 was declared illegal and ineffective; thereafter he has been residing in the suit land by erecting tin-shed house and while he was filling earth to some portion of the suit land, the defendant No.1 issued notice dated 7.4.99 asking him to show cause on what basis he was filling earth on the suit land and also directed him to stop further earth filling; he by letter dated 21.4.1999 replied to said notice dated 7.4.1999 enclosing therewith a copy of the judgment dated 23.3.1992 passed by learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Comilla and also stating that he has not erected any hut in cattle market of Borura as alleged; the defendant No.1 then served the impugned notice dated 12.5.99 directing him to take away his tin-shed from the suit land and hence the suit. The defendants filed written statement stating that the plaintiff has erected tinshed house on the khas property; the lease in favour of the plaintiff has been duly cancelled by order dated 21.7.1976 and Misc. Appeal No.7 of 1976-77 filed by the plaintiff against the above order has also been rejected by A.D.C. (Revenue) and so the plaintiff had no right to stay in the suit land; Title Suit No. 53 of 1985 filed by plaintiff in respect of suit land was dismissed and against the dismissal the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 175 of 1991 which was allowed exparte; the plaintiff has violated the conditions of the lease and the suit land is within the periphery of cattle hut of Borura. The trial court on consideration of the evidence on record found that the notice dated 12.5.1995 is illegal and accordingly decreed the suit. The lower appellate court on due consideration of the evidence on record dismissed the appeal and there-by affirmed the decree passed by the trial court. The High Court Division rejected the revisional application summarily.
